summary_what_it_is: qdrant-memory (Hermes catalog name) = cnkang/hermes-plugin-qdrant-memory: a native Hermes MemoryProvider plugin, MIT, by cnkang (Kang Liu). Per turn, Hermes admits the completed turn into a durable SQLite WAL ledger; async LLM extraction (through Hermes' trusted ctx.llm facade, i.e. the LLM already configured in Hermes) distills facts/preferences/decisions with importance + near-duplicate comparison into an embedded Qdrant collection (qdrant-client LOCAL mode files on disk, no separate service); recall is scoped dense-vector search via 4 agent tools (qdrant_memory_search/_add/_delete) plus a maintenance CLI (status/init/doctor/stats/verify/retry/list/export/migrate). The tweet's claims check out: model extracts facts, new sessions search them, local Qdrant store in Hermes home, in the plugin catalog. Not in the tweet: extraction fires after each primary turn, at session end, and before context compression; payloads are facts (schema-v1), not verbatim turns; embedded mode = qdrant-client local mode, which even Qdrant describes as dev/prototype-grade, and the plugin relies on that (no payload indexes in local mode).

usefulness_verdict.mechanism: Hermes turn -> provider callback sync-commits an event to a SQLite WAL ledger (idempotent, replayable, fail-closed recovery; content-hash tombstones prevent resurrection of deleted facts) -> on one plugin worker: Hermes-configured LLM extracts facts and adjudicates near-duplicates (similarity_review_threshold 0.92, high_similarity 0.97; ADD/SKIP/UPDATE decisions; explicit writes dedupe by canonical text without an LLM) -> stores into Qdrant with named dense vectors + payloads, deterministic content-hash IDs, and an embedding fingerprint that fails closed on pipeline changes (model/dim change forces a new collection)). Extraction hooks: after each primary-agent turn, session end, and before compression; bot/non-primary turns excluded; recalled content treated as untrusted data. Extraction LLM routing: inherit Hermes' model (default), task mode via auxiliary.qdrant_memory_extraction in Hermes config, or operator-approved override. Sources: catalog page, docs/configuration.md, docs/architecture.md, docs/validation.md, docs/security.md.
usefulness_verdict.embedding_and_search_model: Default embedding: local Ollama qwen3-embedding:4b, 2560 dimensions, Cosine, batch 32 (2.5 GB download, 4.02B params, Q4_K_M per Ollama). Or ANY OpenAI-compatible /v1/embeddings endpoint (provider openai-compatible, EMBEDDING_API_KEY, keyed endpoints must use HTTPS). Search is dense-only in this preview - NO hybrid (dense+BM25), no rerank; top_k 8, min_score deliberately unset until calibrated; v0.1.0 notes say quality figures are synthetic regression baselines, not production recall claims. Do NOT confuse with other same-flavored projects: catalog 'qdrant' (kuehnberger) and a qdrant-labs fastembed draft also target Hermes memory.
usefulness_verdict.adds_over_builtin: Built-in = MEMORY.md 2,200 chars + USER.md 1,375 chars hard-budgeted and injected every turn + session_search (SQLite FTS5 exact-text transcript recall). qdrant-memory adds: (1) unbounded long-term fact store that does not compete with the 2,200-char budget; (2) SEMANTIC search over facts - the main gap vs FTS5 word matching; (3) automatic extraction including PRE-COMPRESSION capture (rescues facts compression would discard, same idea as ByteRover); (4) memory lifecycle the built-in lacks: provenance, exact-ID update, per-ID delete with tombstones, scoped delete-all, portable export; (5) the same destination reachable from other agents via standalone CLI/stdio MCP or a shared Qdrant Server/Cloud. Skills and session_search are orthogonal and unaffected. What it does NOT add: hybrid search, rerank, knowledge graphs (Mem0/Hindsight do that); built-in memory still runs alongside (Hermes docs: providers never replace built-in; only ONE external provider active at a time).

disk_bloat_verdict.growth_model_and_scale_estimate: Growth is sublinear in conversation volume because only extracted, deduplicated facts land in Qdrant, while the ledger keeps one row per ADMITTED TURN whose identity/status/manifest rows are retained forever after body scrubbing ('Rows and manifests have no time-based expiry'). Two on-disk stores: <HERMES_HOME>/qdrant-memory/qdrant (embedded collection files) and <HERMES_HOME>/qdrant-memory/state.db (+WAL). Per-point cost at default 2560-dim float32: 10,240 B vector + ~1.5 KB payload x1.5 local-mode overhead ~ 17.6 KB/point (dims verified; payload/overhead assumed). Ledger retention measured at ~1.4 KB per admitted op even after scrub (100k-op synthetic = 138,493,952 B db). Facts/day in the wild is unmeasured, so the estimate brackets it.
disk_bloat_verdict.quantified_estimate: Computed model (2560x4B=10.24KB vector + 1.5KB payload, x1.5 overhead; 1.4KB ledger identity per turn at 5 turns/fact): moderate 20 facts/day ~ 171 MB/year; heavy 100/day ~ 854 MB/year (vectors alone 5.99 GB over 10y; total ~8.3 GB/10y); very heavy 300/day ~ 2.6 GB/year. Measured worst-case transient: WAL ~133 MB with a 100,000-op pending backlog, checkpointed away at close. Importer cost for the legacy 53,861-chunk OpenClaw SQLite: ~906 MB (vectors alone 526 MB). Verdict: non-issue on the 1TB SSD at realistic rates; even a decade of heavy use stays single-digit GB. Labeled assumptions: facts/day rate, 1.5KB payload, 5:1 turn:fact ratio, 1.5x overhead are estimates; only dims, 1.4KB/op ledger identity and the 133MB WAL benchmark are measured.
disk_bloat_verdict.lifecycle_controls: v0.1.0/0.2.x implements NO automatic retention compaction ('It requires a separate design' - operations.md). Manual controls: qdrant_memory_delete per exact ID (content-hash tombstone, fenced against resurrection); CLI delete-all (single scope or --all-agents, fail-closed resumable); init --existing clear destination reset; list/export then re-import; Qdrant-side deletion via its own flow. time_decay_half_life_days exists but is RESERVED policy (no effect). Dedupe thresholds are the main natural brake. Ops doc mandates disk alert at 70%, monitoring state.db/state.db-wal, notes SQLite may reuse freed pages without shrinking and that VACUUM/backups are NOT secure erasure, and says never delete state.db to recover.
disk_bloat_verdict.ram_implications: Embedded mode = qdrant-client local mode INSIDE the Hermes process: no extra daemon (best case for the 16 GB box) but single-client (stop Hermes before CLI maintenance). Rough resident working set ~10 KB/point: a heavy year (~36,500 points) ~ 365 MB - tolerable. The REAL RAM cost is the default embedder: Ollama serving qwen3-embedding:4b = 2.5 GB GGUF (4.02B Q4_K_M) plus Ollama runtime overhead, stacked on gemma + n8n. Configure away: point `embedding` at a smaller Ollama embedder (e.g. nomic-embed-text, 768 dims) via the OpenAI-compatible provider knob (untested combo - verify at install), or batch embeddings off-hours. Alternative: qdrant.mode server (docker, data on the 1TB SSD) = separate resident Qdrant daemon with its own working set (RSS unquantified in project docs - unknown); only worth it for multi-client needs.

integration_verdict.install_mechanism: Official Hermes plugin mechanism: hermes plugins install qdrant-memory -> hermes plugins enable qdrant-memory -> hermes memory setup -> hermes config set memory.provider qdrant-memory -> hermes qdrant-memory init. Install resolves the catalog's reviewed pin, prints declared tools/requirements/known issues before cloning; enable prepares deps via Hermes PM. Requires Python 3.11+, Hermes >= v0.21.5. Version-locked variant: hermes plugins install <github-url> --ref <40-char SHA>, or git clone into $HERMES_HOME/plugins. Outside Hermes: standalone runtime `pip install 'hermes-plugin-qdrant-memory[mcp]==0.2.2'` (CLI `qdrant-memory` + stdio MCP subcommand, no Hermes needed) and metadata-only MCP distro qdrant-memory-mcp==0.1.2 (uvx-able; 4 scoped tools). Settings in <HERMES_HOME>/qdrant-memory.json (0600); secrets via QDRANT_URL/QDRANT_API_KEY/EMBEDDING_API_KEY through Hermes' secret scope.
integration_verdict.in_official_catalog: YES - verified on the official docs domain: Plugin Catalog / Memory / qdrant-memory, by cnkang, added Oct 10 2026, updated Oct 14 2026, with the hermes plugins install copy block, tool list, 'Open in Hermes Desktop', README pinned 'From the reviewed commit e14adc0' (author page shows the entry first listed Oct 10, 2026). Catalog keeps its own reviewed immutable pin (5ec9cac tested Oct 11; e14adc0 README section dated Runtime 0.2.1); PyPI releases do NOT auto-upgrade the pin; the entry description still carries the 'v0.1.0 - limited technical preview' framing while the repo is at Runtime 0.2.2.
integration_verdict.compatibility_with_builtin: Designed to coexist: it registers a native MemoryProvider; Hermes docs state external providers always run ALONGSIDE built-in MEMORY.md/USER.md (never replacing) with only ONE external provider active at a time. The plugin mirrors builtin-memory tool writes into Qdrant (v0.1.0 highlights: 'builtin-memory mirroring'; builtin replace/remove matches exact metadata.previous_content). Skills and session_search subsystems are untouched (different layer, profile-scoped). Caveats for this setup: one writer per destination across all profiles/hosts (writer leases are per-profile-home and do not coordinate - fine for a single-profile setup); embedded mode = sole client (stop Hermes for maintenance); changing scope does not migrate records; requires Hermes >= v0.21.5.
integration_verdict.import_export_existing_memory: Both directions in Mem0-JSON format: `hermes qdrant-memory export` emits a portable JSON document the Mem0 importer accepts (imports re-embed; covers stored memories only, not ledger/recovery state), and `migrate mem0` imports Mem0 exports (JSON or Qdrant sources; read-only, dry-run, resumable, verified by ID/scope/payload hash). MEMORY.md/USER.md markdown: NO documented importer - hand-feed via qdrant_memory_add or convert to the export JSON format (each item re-embeds). The legacy OpenClaw SQLite (~53,861 chunks): no direct importer; the plausible path is a script converting chunks -> export-JSON -> migrate mem0 --resume, cost ~906 MB plus a long local re-embedding run (~1,700 batches of 32 through qwen3-embedding:4b) - treat as a later offline project, not a blocker. Raw qdrant-client bulk-writes bypass the ledger and are not recommended (break idempotency/fingerprints). Round-trip out via export works anytime.

Repo: created 2026-10-06, MIT, Python, not archived, pushed 2026-10-14 (actively developed). 163 commits by cnkang + 4 by dependabot; 4 stars, 0 forks, 1 issue total / 0 open. Releases: v0.1.0 (Oct 10) -> v0.2.2 (Oct 14), 4 releases in 4 days. red_flags: Single author, 4 stars, 11 days old - bus factor ~0 and no third-party battle testing yet (163/163 human commits by cnkang, 0 forks, 1 issue ever)

Self-labeled 'limited technical preview' with real boundaries: one writer per destination across all profiles/hosts, dense-only search (no hybrid/rerank), no web UI, multi-writer Server/Cloud not supported

No automatic retention compaction; ledger identity rows, manifests and tombstones never expire - ops doc tells you to plan capacity, set a 70% disk alert and treat db/WAL/backups as sensitive conversation data (mitigated: tiny identity residue ~1.4 KB/op, and export/delete-all exist)

Default embedding is heavy for this box: qwen3-embedding:4b = 2.5 GB model per Ollama; on 16 GB with n8n + Ollama-gemma already resident it competes for real RAM - swap to a smaller embedder via the openai-compatible knob before adopting

Extraction LLM 'may be a remote provider': by default conversation text goes to whatever LLM Hermes is configured with (a cloud provider here), so privacy-sensitive turns leave the machine unless auxiliary.qdrant_memory_extraction is routed to a local model (author warns slow local models can time out the auxiliary call; timeout configurable, retry via hermes qdrant-memory retry)
No in-place re-embedding: changing embedding model/dimensions fails closed and requires a new collection + explicit migration (schema lock-in as the store grows)

Name-collision minefield: at least four similarly-named Qdrant-memory projects for Hermes (catalog slug 'qdrant-memory' = cnkang; catalog 'qdrant' = kuehnberger; qdrant-labs/hermes-agent-memory-qdrant fastembed draft; glasschan skill; plus cnkang/qdrant-memory-mcp MCP distro) - make sure install targets the catalog slug
